Generated by `junction notifications --app src/app.ts --services src/services`. **Do not edit.**

What this app can tell somebody. Read off a built app, because a notification
registers itself by being autoloaded and takes its type from its own file name —
neither is visible in any one source file.

A notification that stops being registered does not go quiet: it throws at the
moment somebody was owed a message, usually inside a job, long after the deploy
that dropped it. That is what this file is for — the change becomes a diff.

**The type is persisted.** It is written into `notifications.type` and read back
by the browser to choose a renderer, so a type that moves here orphans every row
already written under the old string. Renaming the file renames the type; `type:`
on the definition is what holds it still.

| Type | Transports |

| `OrderConfirmation` | `email` |
| `OrderPaid` | `inApp` |

2 notification(s).

Which transports a given send *uses* is not here: `via` is a function of the
payload and the recipient, so it is a runtime answer. This is the set each
definition can format for.
